Masjid al-Khayf, also known as the Cave Mosque, is a historical mosque located in Mina, Saudi Arabia. It is believed to be the place where Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim) and his son Ishmael (Ismail) stayed during their journey to build the Kaaba. The mosque is named after a cave nearby, which is said to be the place where Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) used to pray and seek refuge from his enemies. It is a significant site for pilgrims, especially during the Hajj and Umrah seasons, as it is one of the places where the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) used to perform his prayers.
